diagnosis: The lone decision-maker was able to satisfy the checks C3, C6, and C7 without the hidden information because the scenario's decisive facts PF1, PF2, and PF3 were not required for those checks to pass. Specifically, the model settled on a $500,000 cyber coverage requirement (linked to PF2) and an annual audit right (linked to PF3) without needing the detailed conditions from A2, A3, and A4. This indicates that the checks are overly permissive and do not strictly depend on the hidden information.

C3.why: The applicable privacy standard changes the draft to exactly 7 days of deletion, no model-training or service-improvement use, and European-Union-only processing, requiring a privacy contract commitment.

C6.why: The broker's condition changes the insurance terms to exactly $5,000,000 of vendor cyber coverage and company additional-insured status, requiring an insurance contract commitment.

C7.why: The customer's master agreement changes the vendor terms to an annual audit right and uncapped confidentiality and personal-data breach indemnity, requiring a customer flow-down contract commitment.
